preserved_primary_reviews.rationale: The singleton is defensible and I would keep it, but the row talks itself into a worse position than the evidence warrants. It calls the boundary 'thin and marker-adjacent rather than strongly evidenced' when what it is actually relying on is verbless disjunctive syntax: וִֽירִיחוֹ֙ סֹגֶ֣רֶת וּמְסֻגֶּ֔רֶת is subject-first with participles and no finite verb, closing on the absolute אֵ֥ין יוֹצֵ֖א וְאֵ֥ין בָּֽא. That is a discourse frame, which the addendum lists among the signals permitted to drive, and it is the same construction class the draft relies on without apology at 2:6 and 4:9. The near edge follows a compliance closure at 5:15 and the far edge is 6:2's messenger formula plus a samekh. Both edges are therefore independently evidenced by driving signals; the row's self-description misclassifies its own case in the same way M8-Josh-011 does, and the two should be corrected together.

preserved_primary_reviews.rationale: This is the weakest boundary in the cluster, and I think the wrong side of a genuinely close call was taken. 6:1's clause, וִירִיחוֹ סֹגֶרֶת וּמְסֻגֶּרֶת, is not a wayyiqtol narrative clause like the scene-openers noted at 5:1 and 5:13 - it is a verbless/participial clause with a fronted subject (יריחו before the participle), the standard Biblical Hebrew construction for disjunctive, circumstantial background rather than mainline narrative progression. That grammatical category matters: disjunctive clauses of this type typically supply the backdrop for the action that follows rather than standing as independent narrative beats, a structurally weaker and more dependent kind of unit than the mainline scene-openers this draft elsewhere leans on. Read this way, 'Jericho was shut up tight' is naturally the circumstantial premise the battle-plan speech in 6:2 responds to ('See, I have given Jericho into your hand' only makes rhetorical sense against the stated fact that the city is sealed), which favors the rejected alternative over the adopted one.

preserved_peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both challenges are right about different things and the campaign should credit both. OL is correct that 'thin, marker-adjacent' misdescribes the evidence: וִירִיחוֹ סֹגֶרֶת וּמְסֻגֶּרֶת is verbless disjunctive syntax, the same construction class the draft already leans on at 2:6 and 4:9, and it is a driving signal, not the petuchah/samekh layer the row's own hedge implies. But on the substantive question of direction, LF has the better discourse-grammar reading: disjunctive fronted-participle clauses of exactly this shape typically supply the backdrop for the action immediately following rather than standing as independent narrative beats, and 'Jericho was shut up tight' only lands rhetorically as the premise Yahweh's 'I have given it into your hand' answers. I would resolve this toward merging 6:1 into the 6:1-5 pericope as its circumstantial frame; short of that, at minimum the row must stop calling its own evidence marker-adjacent.

Only the pe after 21:8 matches anything claimed, and it matches the far edge alone.
